parts.title: The baker's day
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Mina's alarm rings at three in the morning, when most people are fast asleep. By four, she is in the kitchen of the bakery where she works, with flour on her hands and the first dough in the mixer. "The secret of good bread is time," she says. "You cannot hurry it."

The dough must rest for several hours, so Mina works on different recipes while she waits. She makes croissants, which need three days of preparation, and heavy brown loaves with seeds. At six, the shop opens, and the first customers arrive. Some of them stand outside before the door is even open.

Mina loves the smell of fresh bread, but the work is tiring. Her back hurts, and the oven burns her arms. She finishes at noon and usually goes straight to bed. "I miss parties and late nights," she admits, "but I would not change my job for anything."

Her favourite moment comes at seven, when a little boy comes in each day and asks for a roll. He says that Mina's bread tastes of sunshine.

parts.title: The story of bread
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Bread is one of the oldest foods in the world. [1] Archaeologists have found traces of flat bread that is more than fourteen thousand years old.

The first loaves were hard and flat. [2] Then, about six thousand years ago, the Egyptians discovered that a mixture of flour and water, left in the warm sun, began to swell.

This was the beginning of yeast. [3] The loaves became soft, light and much tastier, and bakers started to open shops.

In the Middle Ages, the baker was an important person in every town. [4] Cheating the customers, for example by making loaves smaller, was a serious crime.

Today, bread is eaten almost everywhere. [5] From French baguettes to Indian naan, every country has its own favourite kind.
sentences: Nobody knows exactly where it was first made.
The laws about bread were strict.
People ground grain into powder and cooked it on hot stones.

gaps.explanation: Nobody knows where it was first made; the next sentence says traces have been found.
People ground grain and cooked it on hot stones; the next sentence says that later the Egyptians discovered yeast.
Yeast makes the dough rise; the next sentence says the loaves became soft and light.
The laws were strict; the next sentence gives cheating customers as a crime.
It takes many different forms; the next sentence gives examples from France and India.

parts.passage: Hi Elmer, I am having a wonderful time in Paris. This morning, I went [1] a little bakery near my hotel and bought a croissant. It was still warm, [2] it tasted amazing. The baker spoke to me in French, [3] I did not understand a word! I just smiled and pointed. Tomorrow, I am going to a baking class, [4] I hope to learn how to make baguettes. I will bring some home, [5] they might not stay fresh until I arrive. Let [6] know when you are free. Hank

parts.title: Making bread at home
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Making bread at home is easier than you think. All you need [1] flour, water, salt and yeast. First, mix everything together in a large bowl. Then, push and fold the dough with your hands for ten minutes. This is the most tiring part, [2] it is also the most important. Put the dough in a warm place and cover it with a cloth. [3] about an hour, it should be twice as big. After that, shape the dough into a round loaf and put it on a tray. Bake it in a hot oven for forty minutes. The smell will fill your house, [4] you will want to eat it at once. Wait [5] least ten minutes before cutting it, or the inside will be too soft. If you do not like white bread, you can add seeds [6] a spoonful of honey.

gaps.explanation: All you need is: singular verb after the clause.
But shows contrast between tiring and important.
After about an hour introduces the time.
And joins the results: smell fills the house and you want to eat it.
At least is a fixed phrase for a minimum.
Seeds or honey gives two alternatives.

parts.title: A talk about a bakery tour
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Hello, everybody, and welcome to Rose Bakery. My name is Lev, and I will be your guide today. The bakery was founded in nineteen forty-eight by Rose Walker, and it is still run by her family. We make about two thousand loaves every day. The kitchen is very hot, so please do not touch the ovens. First, we will see the dough room, and then we will visit the packing area. After the tour, you can taste a free roll with butter in our cafe. If you like the bread, you can buy it in the shop at a ten per cent discount. Please remember that photographs are not allowed in the kitchen, but you can take as many as you like in the garden. The tour takes forty-five minutes.

gaps.explanation: She says the bakery was founded in nineteen forty-eight.

gaps.explanation: She says visitors can taste a free roll with butter.

gaps.explanation: She says there is a ten per cent discount.

parts.title: An interview with a young baker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Mirko, you opened your own bakery at nineteen. Why?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I could not find a job, so I decided to create one. My aunt lent me her old kitchen, and I started with ten loaves a day.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was the first year like?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Terrible and wonderful. I worked fourteen hours a day, and I lost a lot of money. But on the last day of the year, people brought me presents.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What kind of bread do you make?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Mostly sourdough, which needs a special mixture that I have fed every day for six years. I call it Bernard.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You gave your mixture a name?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Of course. It is alive, so it deserves one. If I go on holiday, my sister looks after Bernard.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What would you say to other young people?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Start small, ask for advice, and be ready for mistakes. My first loaf looked like a rock.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Where do you see yourself in ten years?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: In a bigger bakery with a school attached, so I can teach children how to make bread.
